question.problem:
A certain store sells three types of instant soups: chicken, meat, and vegetable. The following table describes how the number of customers changes between the three types of instant soups each month:
From:
Chicken Meat Vegetable
To: Chicken $0.4$ $0.2$ $0.3$
Meat $0.3$ $0.4$ $0.2$
Vegetable $0.3$ $0.4$ $0.5$
For example, $30%$ of chicken soup customers switch to vegetable each month, and $20%$ of vegetable customers switch to meat. Currently, $400$ customers buy chicken soup, $400$ customers buy meat soup, and $200$ customers buy vegetable soup. How many customers will purchase vegetable instant soup in one month? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.

current_example.problem:
A certain industry produces $2$ types of sugar, namely sugar $A$ and sugar $B$. The following table describes how the number of consumers changes between both types of sugar in a month:
From:
Sugar $A$ Sugar $B$
To: Sugar $A$ $0.3$ $0.45$
Sugar $B$ $0.7$ $0.55$
That is, $70\%$ of sugar $A$ customers switch to sugar $B$ each month, and $45\%$ of sugar $B$ customers switch to sugar $A.$ Currently, $600$ customers use sugar $A,$ while $400$ customers use sugar $B.$ How many customers will use sugar $A$ in one month? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.
current_example.worked_solution:
From the table, we can build the corresponding stochastic matrix: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228502/assets/fcf892ba52d299d61b2cfea012fe95ee37b1b1fa1c7482000ecc3e3ded22de24.svg)

The vector describing the number of customers for each type of sugar is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228502/assets/8718200a69a5cdc26f86e99d26218c9c0e776b6cdab218a08c7726f0de8fce30.svg)
Dividing the vector above by the total number of customers $(1\,000),$ we get the stochastic vector of the initial state:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228502/assets/a876243cca8f378b9e77570c4a20b196e87da5200f2640655abd013ae702194d.svg)

To find the state vector $\mathbf{x}_1$ after one month, we apply one step of the Markov chain:

$$
\mathbf{x}_1=P\mathbf{x}_0
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =P{x}_{0} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.3 & 0.45 \\ 0.7 & 0.55\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0.6 \\ 0.4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.36 \\ 0.64\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, after one month, $\color{blue}36\%$ of customers will use sugar $A.$ Computing $36\%$ of $1\,000,$ we obtain

$$
1\,000 \cdot 0.36 = 360.
$$

Therefore, $360$ customers will use sugar $A$ in one month.
